# QuotaPin 1.1.2

QuotaPin 1.1.2 keeps long-running quota honest and adds a true full-width account-row quota line.

- **Durable live recovery:** Windows tray, Windows quiet watcher, and the macOS watcher can resume an exited Agent against the same verified Codex session with bounded backoff—without reopening or restarting Codex.
- **No frozen percentage:** the renderer receives a lightweight heartbeat. If delivery disappears, the old value is replaced by an unavailable state instead of remaining on screen as if it were current.
- **App Server self-healing:** repeated read or initialization timeouts retire the dead child and continue bounded recovery rather than exhausting a permanent retry budget.
- **Two quota-line widths:** Quick can keep the line under the visible quota modules or stretch it across the usable account row. Legacy stops before Codex Help; Beta uses the complete expanded row.
- **Update supervision preserved:** a command-mode hot update republishes exact watcher ownership for the resumed Agent. Guided installs remain tray-owned, and saved settings stay intact.
- **Smaller macOS delivery:** launcher and Agent now share one universal self-contained host instead of packaging two complete runtimes. Upgrades stop only the exact previous Agent before the atomic swap.
- **Bounded remote documents:** update metadata and loopback CDP target lists are byte-limited and strictly decoded before JSON parsing.
- **No forced Codex restart:** updates reconnect only to the exact verified running process. If verification fails, the new version waits for the next normal launch.

Windows Quick Start:

The guided Windows package is `QuotaPin-1.1.2.exe`.

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WSL043/QuotaPin-for-Codex/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

macOS Quick Start:

The macOS package is `QuotaPin-macOS-1.1.2.dmg`.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WSL043/QuotaPin-for-Codex/main/install-macos.sh | bash
```

Windows requires x64 Windows 10 version 2004 or later; Windows 11 is verified and Windows 10 remains best effort. Windows ARM64 is not supported. The macOS package is ad-hoc signed and CI-validated; signed-in real-device and Gatekeeper acceptance remains provisional.
